newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil decree restricts court powers over pay.
newsitem.headline: Brazil decree restricts court powers over pay.

text.p: Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso has signed a decree that restricts the powers of courts to issue public sector pay rises, a presidential official said.

The decree would also make it harder for individuals or groups to seek injunctions that might hurt public finances, as in the case of suits against privatizations, Gilmar Mendes, deputy head of the presidency's legal department said.

The decree would have an immediate effect on ongoing court cases brought by tens of thousands of civil servants who claim they are entitled to a 28.9 percent pay increase awarded to 11 federal workers by the supreme court earlier this year, he said.

The 11 successfully claimed they were entitled to a 28.9 percent pay rise given to the armed forces in 1993, citing a rule that entitles one category of public sector worker to pay rises awarded to others.
The supreme court ruling was widely considered to have set a precedent for the entire federal workforce and pensioners, jeopardising the government's attempts to cut public spending.
The decree would prevent judges from provisionally awarding pay increases to public sector workers before reaching a final verdict on the merit of the increase in each specific case, Mendes said.
Provisional increases had already been awarded to groups of workers seeking the 28.9 percent raise, he said.
"The decree allows a more rational approach to cases and avoids a generalization which has been the case," Mendes said.
The decree would also require judges to ask for financial or property guarantees from individuals or groups seeking injunctions that could have a negative impact on public finances.

The guarantee requirement would apply to requests for injunctions to halt the government's privatization program, Mendes said. "It will encourage the judgement of cases in a responsible way," he said.
